references.text: Moses asks who he is to go to Pharaoh, which shows his humility and lack of self-exaltation.
Moses claims that he is not eloquent and asks God to send someone else, demonstrating his humble attitude.
The humble (עֲנָוִים) shall inherit the land and rejoice in great peace. The same Hebrew root as 'ענו' is used here.
The Lord guides the humble (עֲנָוִים) in what is right and teaches them his way.
Humility goes before honor, reflecting Moses' character as the most humble of all people.
Humility and fear of the Lord bring wealth, honor, and life.
God looks to the one who is poor and crushed in spirit, who trembles at his word.
God will leave a humble and lowly people in Israel who shall take refuge in the name of the Lord.
Jesus says that the meek (πραεῖς) shall inherit the earth, a direct parallel to the humility described about Moses.
Jesus describes himself as meek (πραΰς) and humble in heart, the same quality that characterized Moses.
Paul appeals by the meekness (πραΰτητος) and gentleness of Christ.
An exhortation to humility and to regard others as more important than oneself, similar to Moses' character.
